title: Zanzibar Stone Town Flatbread
community: Zanzibar Stone Town — the sesame flatbread tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Mkate wa Ufuta — a soft, slightly sweet flatbread crusted with sesame seeds on one side, pan-fried until golden. Zanzibar Stone Town's morning bread — softer than chapati, thicker than injera, and unmistakably sesame-fragrant.
longDesc: Mkate wa Ufuta is the Stone Town morning flatbread — distinct from chapati by its thickness, its slight sweetness, and most importantly its sesame seed crust. It is the bread that vendors sell from baskets in the narrow lanes of Stone Town each morning.
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Add oil and warm water. Mix to a soft dough.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each into a round about 8mm thick.
Press one side firmly into sesame seeds.
Cook sesame-side down in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes.
chefTips: The sesame crust goes down first — maximum contact time with the pan.
Thicker than chapati — allow enough time.
commonMistakes: Too thin — loses its characteristic thickness.
cookingScience: Sesame seeds pressed firmly into the dough surface become embedded as the dough cooks — the starch on the dough surface gelatinises and bonds with the sesame protein, effectively gluing the seeds in place.
healthBenefits: Sesame seeds add calcium and zinc.
culturalNote: Mkate wa Ufuta is the bread of Zanzibar's mornings — sold from baskets by women in the narrow lanes of Stone Town, bought by commuters and students before the day begins. Its sesame fragrance is the first smell of a Stone Town morning.
